newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-ELTSOVA AND BUSHKOV LEAD PAIRS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELTSOVA AND BUSHKOV LEAD PAIRS.

text.p: World champions Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov of Russia seized the lead in the short programme of the pairs event at the European figure skating championships on Tuesday.
The 1993 European winners, skating second last of the 17 couples, produced a slick programme packed with interesting moves to nose out Germany's 1995 champions Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer.
The Russian couple were beaten three times by the Germans in Champions Series events this season but Eltsova said she and her partner had no thought of revenge on Tuesday.
"Sometimes they win, sometimes we win, sometimes someone else wins. That's skating," she said.
Woetzel, second with her partner in last season's European and world championships, felt no frustration at standing second again.
"Second is a great place," she said. "We gave all we could give and it was the best we could have done."
There was little to choose between the two excellent, error-free routines, but six of the nine judges preferred the Russians. The three others picked the Germans.
Sarah Abitbol and Stephane Bernadis of France held third spot, which was their finishing position last year.
The medals will be decided in the free skating on Wednesday night and whichever of the leading three couples wins that section, which is worth two-thirds of the total marks, will be the champions.

The best-looking programme of the night came from former world champions Evgenia Shishkova and Vadim Naumov of Russia but it was marred when Shishkova lost balance landing a triple toe loop jump and touched both hands to the ice.
Naumov broke his left shoulder last October and was off the ice for several weeks for surgery, having a pin removed just before the NHK Trophy event in December.
Last year's winners, Russians Oksana Kazakova and Artur Dmitriev, are not taking part because they finished only fourth in last month's national championships.
